messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 at 99-100% GPU utilization. Queue length=1187, avg latency per request rising. Trigger: gpu_pool_util_high. Paging oncall: maria (oncall)

maria (oncall): ack. i'm looking. assigning kevin for autoscaler logs. tagging acmehealth account manager.

kevin (infra): I see a surge from tenant AcmeHealthInc - reserved GPUs fully consumed. Autoscaler tried to scale but saw repeated failures: 'scale request rejected: poolScaleLimitReached' and API 429 from cloud provider.

jess (sre): copying autoscaler logs now. one-line:

```
2026-03-15T02:14:03Z ERROR scale_loop.go: failed to increase pool: api error 429: quotaExceeded rateLimitExceeded
2026-03-15T02:14:04Z WARN  scheduler.go: scale-request queued (id=abc123) but rejected: poolMax=16 current=16
2026-03-15T02:14:10Z INFO  eviction.go: marking candidate noisy-tenant AcmeHealthInc for soft-eviction check
```

maria (oncall): poolMax is 16 here. any reason that's set so low? policy should have allowed burst=4.

tom (platform): config shows max=16, burst disabled due to a previous experiment (burst-allocator=false). I can flip it but need to coordinate - might cause transient VM churn.

jess (sre): customer impact: AcmeHealthInc saw request failures and increased tail latency; other tenants on the same pool seeing throttling and queue growth. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) enable hosted fallback for AcmeHealthInc (failover-hosted route), 2) apply per-tenant soft concurrency cap 3) re-enable burst allocator and raise poolMax to 24.

kevin (infra): Trying to call autoscaler API to bump max to 24 now:
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  https://internal-api.redwood/scheduler/pools/eu-west-1-dedicated-42/scale -d '{"poolMax":24}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy request submitted: scale-change-1999 by kevin. CI check: config-validation passed.

kevin (infra): API returned 429 again. provider quota appears exhausted in eu-west-1 for the VM type (a100-40gb). Opening cloud console ticket.

maria (oncall): ok, fallback plan: jess, can you apply a routing override for AcmeHealthInc to sent their traffic to hosted fallback? tom, reduce per-tenant concurrency for that tenant to 20 while we wait.

jess (sre): on it. applying routing override:
```
POST /v1/routing/tenants/AcmeHealthInc/overrides
{ "target": "hosted-fallback-eu", "priority": 100 }
```

jess (sre): override applied. verifying... requests for AcmeHealthInc now show 200->503->200 in logs as new traffic drains.

kevin (infra): cloud provider support responded: temporary quota exhaustion in region, ETA ~ 45 minutes for quota increase after our support case. They suggested migrating some instances to another region but that requires cross-region networking changes.

tom (platform): I just pushed per-tenant concurrency caps for AcmeHealthInc to 20 using the control plane feature flag. That should stop new work from entering the queue for that tenant.

marc (eng): Customer-facing note: I've alerted Acme's ops lead and support; they're aware. requesting their tolerance for short downtime while we move traffic to hosted fallback.

maria (oncall): monitoring dashboards: total queue dropped from 1187 -> 420 in 9 minutes after override and caps. good. but other tenants still seeing higher latency.

jess (sre): also found a noisy-worker pattern (one job from Acme issuing thousands of tiny requests) — added rule to detect and batch these requests on ingress as temporary mitigation.

kevin (infra): cloud quota bumped by provider. retrying scale to 24...

deploy-bot: Scale request completed: poolMax updated to 24. Autoscaler resumed creating nodes.

kevin (infra): new nodes are up, pool GPU utilization dropping to 60-70%. queue at 87 now. routing override continues for safety.

maria (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. brief timeline for follow-up: 
- immediate: Acme traffic routed to hosted fallback, per-tenant cap applied, noisy-worker batching enabled.
- short term (couple hours): re-evaluate whether to evict noisy tenant fully or require them to reduce request rate.
- postmortem: own action items - re-enable burst allocator guardrails, audit poolMax defaults, add automated cloud quota checks and early warnings, add per-tenant request pattern detectors.

tom (platform): will open a changelist to re-enable burst allocator and add a safety throttle to avoid poolMax being left too low by experiments.

jess (sre): I'll draft a customer-facing incident message for AcmeHealthInc and ops.

marc (eng): thanks team. please add any logs/screenshots to the incident tracker and i'll schedule a debrief with account manager.

maria (oncall): closing pager. leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
